544	def _verify_samples(
545	    source_arg: str,
546	    samples_arg: str,
547	    noise_model_arg: str | None,
548	    tolerance: float,
549	    ctx: _RunContext | None = None,
550	) -> int:
551	    # Three inputs may request standard input; at most one may be '-'. The
552	    # conflict is detected before any input is read.
553	    stdin_args = [source_arg, samples_arg]
554	    if noise_model_arg is not None:
555	        stdin_args.append(noise_model_arg)
556	    if sum(value == "-" for value in stdin_args) > 1:
557	        _emit_error(
558	            "verification_error",
559	            "at most one of the circuit source, samples document and noise model "
560	            "can be read from standard input",
561	        )
562	        return 2
563	
564	    # Circuit and noise model use the exact simulate/probabilities path
565	    # (reading, UTF-8, parsing, validation, model normalization).
566	    program, noise_model, error, exit_code = _prepare_simulation(
567	        source_arg, noise_model_arg, ctx=ctx
568	    )
569	    if error is not None:
570	        _emit_error_payload(error)
571	        return exit_code
572	    assert program is not None
573	
574	    samples_text, read_code = _read_samples_document(samples_arg, ctx)
575	    if samples_text is None:
576	        return read_code if read_code is not None else 1
577	
578	    # The samples document is fully validated against the parsed classical
579	    # register width before any state is evolved.
580	    try:
581	        counts = _parse_samples_document(samples_text, program.num_clbits)
582	    except _SampleInputError as exc:
583	        _emit_error("sample_input_error", str(exc))
584	        return 2
585	
586	    # Refuse an input-overwriting export before any state is evolved.
587	    if ctx is not None and (code := _guard_output_conflict(ctx)) is not None:
588	        return code
589	
590	    try:
591	        # Register sizes are capped at 20 (state vector) or
592	        # MAX_NOISE_QUBITS (density matrix) inside the shared core.
593	        basis_probabilities = evolve_basis_probabilities(program, noise_model)
594	    except SimulationError as exc:
595	        _emit_error("simulation_error", str(exc))
596	        return 3
597	
598	    # Expected probabilities follow the exact ``probabilities`` convention
599	    # (aggregation, renormalization, near-zero/near-one snapping).
600	    expected = probability_payload(program, basis_probabilities, noise_model)["probabilities"]
601	    assert isinstance(expected, dict)
602	
603	    shots = sum(counts.values())
604	    observed: dict[str, float] = {}
605	    for key in sorted(counts):
606	        snapped = snap_probability(counts[key] / shots)
607	        if snapped is not None:
608	            observed[key] = snapped
609	
610	    # Total variation distance over the union of both distributions' keys;
611	    # outcomes absent from either side contribute probability zero.
612	    keys = set(expected) | set(observed)
613	    distance = 0.5 * math.fsum(
614	        abs(expected.get(key, 0.0) - observed.get(key, 0.0)) for key in keys
615	    )
616	    accepted = distance <= tolerance
617	
618	    result: dict[str, object] = {
619	        "schema_version": 1,
620	        "num_qubits": program.num_qubits,
621	        "num_clbits": program.num_clbits,
622	        "shots": shots,
623	        "noise_model": noise_model,
624	        "tolerance": tolerance,
625	        "total_variation_distance": distance,
626	        "accepted": accepted,
627	        "expected_probabilities": expected,
628	        "observed_probabilities": observed,
629	    }
630	    return _finish(ctx, result, 0 if accepted else 3)
631

673	def _expectation(
674	    source_arg: str,
675	    observables_arg: str,
676	    noise_model_arg: str | None,
677	    ctx: _RunContext | None = None,
678	) -> int:
679	    # Three inputs may request standard input; at most one may be '-'. The
680	    # conflict is detected before any input is read.
681	    stdin_args = [source_arg, observables_arg]
682	    if noise_model_arg is not None:
683	        stdin_args.append(noise_model_arg)
684	    if sum(value == "-" for value in stdin_args) > 1:
685	        _emit_error(
686	            "expectation_error",
687	            "at most one of the circuit source, observables document and noise model "
688	            "can be read from standard input",
689	        )
690	        return 2
691	
692	    # Circuit and noise model use the exact simulate/probabilities path
693	    # (reading, UTF-8, parsing, validation, model normalization).
694	    program, noise_model, error, exit_code = _prepare_simulation(
695	        source_arg, noise_model_arg, ctx=ctx
696	    )
697	    if error is not None:
698	        _emit_error_payload(error)
699	        return exit_code
700	    assert program is not None
701	
702	    observables_text, read_code = _read_observables_document(observables_arg, ctx)
703	    if observables_text is None:
704	        return read_code if read_code is not None else 1
705	
706	    # The observables document is fully validated against the parsed
707	    # register size before any state is evolved.
708	    try:
709	        observables = parse_observables(observables_text, program.num_qubits)
710	    except ObservableError as exc:
711	        _emit_error("observable_error", str(exc))
712	        return 2
713	
714	    # Refuse an input-overwriting export before any state is evolved.
715	    if ctx is not None and (code := _guard_output_conflict(ctx)) is not None:
716	        return code
717	
718	    if noise_model is None:
719	        # The parser already caps the register at the 20-qubit
720	        # state-vector limit.
721	        state = simulate_state_vector(program)
722	        results = [
723	            {
724	                "id": observable_id,
725	                "expectation": snap_expectation(state_vector_expectation(state, operators)),
726	            }
727	            for observable_id, operators in observables
728	        ]
729	        result: dict[str, object] = {
730	            "schema_version": 1,
731	            "num_qubits": program.num_qubits,
732	            "noise_model": None,
733	            "results": results,
734	        }
735	    else:
736	        if program.num_qubits > MAX_NOISE_QUBITS:
737	            _emit_error(
738	                "simulation_error",
739	                f"noise simulation supports at most {MAX_NOISE_QUBITS} qubits, "
740	                f"got {program.num_qubits}",
741	            )
742	            return 3
743	        rho = normalized_density_matrix(evolve_density_matrix(program, noise_model))
744	        results = [
745	            {
746	                "id": observable_id,
747	                "expectation": snap_expectation(density_matrix_expectation(rho, operators)),
748	            }
749	            for observable_id, operators in observables
750	        ]
751	        result = {
752	            "schema_version": 1,
753	            "num_qubits": program.num_qubits,
754	            "noise_model": noise_model,
755	            "results": results,
756	        }
757	    return _finish(ctx, result, 0)

764	_BATCH_ROOT_KEYS = ("schema_version", "jobs")
765	_BATCH_JOB_KEYS = ("id", "source", "shots", "seed", "noise_model")

768	class _BatchManifestError(Exception):
769	    """The batch manifest is structurally invalid (``batch_input_error``)."""
770	
771	
772	def _manifest_pairs(pairs: list[tuple[str, object]]) -> dict[str, object]:
773	    result: dict[str, object] = {}
774	    for key, value in pairs:
775	        if key in result:
776	            raise _BatchManifestError(f"duplicate key {key!r} in batch manifest")
777	        result[key] = value

781	def _reject_manifest_constant(value: str) -> None:
782	    raise _BatchManifestError(f"batch manifest contains non-JSON constant {value!r}")
783	
784	
785	def _is_json_int(value: object) -> bool:
786	    # bool is a subclass of int but is not a JSON integer here.
787	    return isinstance(value, int) and not isinstance(value, bool)

789	
790	def _validate_batch_manifest(data: object) -> list[dict[str, object]]:
791	    """Validate the parsed manifest, returning the raw jobs in list order.
792	
793	    Every structural, type and range rule is checked here, before any task
794	    file is read. Raises :class:`_BatchManifestError` on the first problem.
795	    """
796	    if not isinstance(data, dict):
797	        raise _BatchManifestError("batch manifest must be a JSON object")
798	
799	    for key in data:
800	        if key not in _BATCH_ROOT_KEYS:
801	            raise _BatchManifestError(f"unknown batch manifest key {key!r}")
802	
803	    if "schema_version" not in data:
804	        raise _BatchManifestError("batch manifest is missing required key 'schema_version'")
805	    schema_version = data["schema_version"]
806	    if not _is_json_int(schema_version) or schema_version != BATCH_SCHEMA_VERSION:
807	        raise _BatchManifestError(
808	            f"batch manifest schema_version must be {BATCH_SCHEMA_VERSION}, got {schema_version!r}"
809	        )
810	
811	    if "jobs" not in data:
812	        raise _BatchManifestError("batch manifest is missing required key 'jobs'")
813	    jobs = data["jobs"]
814	    if not isinstance(jobs, list):
815	        raise _BatchManifestError("batch manifest 'jobs' must be an array")
816	    if not 1 <= len(jobs) <= MAX_BATCH_JOBS:
817	        raise _BatchManifestError(
818	            f"batch manifest 'jobs' must contain between 1 and {MAX_BATCH_JOBS} jobs, got {len(jobs)}"
819	        )
820	
821	    seen_ids: set[str] = set()
822	    for index, job in enumerate(jobs):
823	        where = f"job at jobs[{index}]"
824	        if not isinstance(job, dict):
825	            raise _BatchManifestError(f"{where} must be a JSON object")
826	        for key in job:
827	            if key not in _BATCH_JOB_KEYS:
828	                raise _BatchManifestError(f"{where} has unknown key {key!r}")
829	
830	        if "id" not in job:
831	            raise _BatchManifestError(f"{where} is missing required key 'id'")
832	        job_id = job["id"]
833	        if not isinstance(job_id, str) or not job_id:
834	            raise _BatchManifestError(f"{where} 'id' must be a non-empty string")
835	        if job_id in seen_ids:
836	            raise _BatchManifestError(f"duplicate job id {job_id!r}")
837	        seen_ids.add(job_id)
838	
839	        if "source" not in job:
840	            raise _BatchManifestError(f"{where} is missing required key 'source'")
841	        source = job["source"]
842	        if not isinstance(source, str):
843	            raise _BatchManifestError(f"{where} 'source' must be a string")
844	        if source == "-":
845	            raise _BatchManifestError(f"{where} 'source' must not be '-'; stdin is reserved for the manifest")
846	
847	        if "shots" in job:
848	            shots = job["shots"]
849	            if not _is_json_int(shots) or shots <= 0:
850	                raise _BatchManifestError(f"{where} 'shots' must be a positive integer")
851	
852	        if "seed" in job and not _is_json_int(job["seed"]):
853	            raise _BatchManifestError(f"{where} 'seed' must be an integer")
854	
855	        if "noise_model" in job:
856	            noise_model = job["noise_model"]
857	            if not isinstance(noise_model, str):
858	                raise _BatchManifestError(f"{where} 'noise_model' must be a string path")
859	            if noise_model == "-":
860	                raise _BatchManifestError(
861	                    f"{where} 'noise_model' must not be '-'; stdin is reserved for the manifest"
862	                )
863	
864	    return jobs
865

867	def _batch_simulate(manifest_arg: str, ctx: _RunContext | None = None) -> int:
868	    try:
869	        if manifest_arg == "-":
870	            raw_manifest = sys.stdin.buffer.read()
871	            base_dir = os.getcwd()
872	        else:
873	            with open(manifest_arg, "rb") as handle:
874	                raw_manifest = handle.read()
875	            base_dir = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(manifest_arg))
876	    except OSError as exc:
877	        _emit_error("io_error", f"cannot read manifest {manifest_arg!r}: {exc.strerror or exc}")
878	        return 1

1009	    """Reject non-finite floats anywhere in an already-parsed JSON payload.

1026	def _validate_baseline_output(output: object, where: str) -> dict[str, object]:
1027	    if not isinstance(output, dict):
1028	        raise _ReconcileInputError(f"{where} must be a JSON object")
1029	    for key in output:
1030	        if key not in _OUTPUT_V2_KEYS:
1031	            raise _ReconcileInputError(f"{where} has unknown key {key!r}")
1032	
1033	    for required in _OUTPUT_V1_KEYS:
1034	        if required not in output:
1035	            raise _ReconcileInputError(f"{where} is missing required key {required!r}")
1036	
1037	    schema_version = _require_int(output["schema_version"], f"{where} 'schema_version'")
1038	    shots = _require_int(output["shots"], f"{where} 'shots'")
1039	    seed = _require_int(output["seed"], f"{where} 'seed'")
1040	    num_qubits = _require_int(output["num_qubits"], f"{where} 'num_qubits'")
1041	    num_clbits = _require_int(output["num_clbits"], f"{where} 'num_clbits'")
1042	
1043	    if schema_version not in (1, 2):
1044	        raise _ReconcileInputError(f"{where} 'schema_version' must be 1 or 2")
1045	    if shots <= 0:
1046	        raise _ReconcileInputError(f"{where} 'shots' must be a positive integer")
1047	    if not 1 <= num_qubits <= 20:
1048	        raise _ReconcileInputError(f"{where} 'num_qubits' must be between 1 and 20")
1049	    if not 1 <= num_clbits <= 20:
1050	        raise _ReconcileInputError(f"{where} 'num_clbits' must be between 1 and 20")
1051	
1052	    counts = output["counts"]
1053	    if not isinstance(counts, dict) or not counts:
1054	        raise _ReconcileInputError(f"{where} 'counts' must be a non-empty JSON object")
1055	    total = 0
1056	    for key, value in counts.items():
1057	        if not isinstance(key, str) or not key:
1058	            raise _ReconcileInputError(f"{where} 'counts' keys must be non-empty strings")
1059	        if not _is_json_int(value) or value <= 0:
1060	            raise _ReconcileInputError(f"{where} 'counts' values must be positive integers")
1061	        if len(key) != num_clbits or any(bit not in "01" for bit in key):
1062	            raise _ReconcileInputError(
1063	                f"{where} 'counts' key {key!r} is not a {num_clbits}-bit measurement string"
1064	            )
1065	        total += value
1066	    if total != shots:
1067	        raise _ReconcileInputError(f"{where} 'counts' must sum to shots ({shots}), got {total}")
1068	
1069	    if schema_version == 2:
1070	        if num_qubits > MAX_NOISE_QUBITS:
1071	            raise _ReconcileInputError(
1072	                f"{where} noisy output must have at most {MAX_NOISE_QUBITS} qubits"
1073	            )
1074	        if "noise_model" not in output:
1075	            raise _ReconcileInputError(f"{where} is missing required key 'noise_model'")
1076	        noise_model = output["noise_model"]
1077	        if not isinstance(noise_model, dict) or not noise_model:
1078	            raise _ReconcileInputError(f"{where} 'noise_model' must be a non-empty JSON object")
1079	        for channel, probability in noise_model.items():
1080	            if channel not in _NOISE_CHANNELS:
1081	                raise _ReconcileInputError(f"{where} has unknown noise channel {channel!r}")
1082	            if isinstance(probability, bool) or not isinstance(probability, (int, float)):
1083	                raise _ReconcileInputError(f"{where} noise channel {channel!r} must be a number")
1084	            if not math.isfinite(float(probability)) or not 0.0 <= float(probability) <= 1.0:
1085	                raise _ReconcileInputError(
1086	                    f"{where} noise channel {channel!r} probability must be between 0 and 1"
1087	                )

1089	        raise _ReconcileInputError(f"{where} schema_version 1 output must not contain 'noise_model'")

1091	    return output

1120	def _validate_baseline(data: object, jobs: list[dict[str, object]]) -> list[dict[str, object]]:
1121	    """Validate the batch-result *data* against the manifest *jobs*.
1122	
1123	    Self-consistency and correspondence (count, ids, order) are checked
1124	    here, before any task is re-run. Raises :class:`_ReconcileInputError`.
1125	    """
1126	    if not isinstance(data, dict):
1127	        raise _ReconcileInputError("baseline must be a JSON object")
1128	    for key in data:
1129	        if key not in _BASELINE_ROOT_KEYS:
1130	            raise _ReconcileInputError(f"unknown baseline key {key!r}")
1131	    if any(key not in data for key in _BASELINE_ROOT_KEYS):
1132	        raise _ReconcileInputError("baseline is missing one or more required root keys")
1133	
1134	    schema_version = _require_int(data["schema_version"], "baseline 'schema_version'")
1135	    if schema_version != BATCH_SCHEMA_VERSION:
1136	        raise _ReconcileInputError(
1137	            f"baseline schema_version must be {BATCH_SCHEMA_VERSION}, got {schema_version!r}"
1138	        )
1139	
1140	    job_count = _require_int(data["job_count"], "baseline 'job_count'")
1141	    succeeded = _require_int(data["succeeded"], "baseline 'succeeded'")
1142	    failed = _require_int(data["failed"], "baseline 'failed'")
1143	    if job_count < 0 or succeeded < 0 or failed < 0:
1144	        raise _ReconcileInputError("baseline counters must be non-negative")
1145	    if succeeded + failed != job_count:
1146	        raise _ReconcileInputError("baseline 'succeeded' + 'failed' must equal 'job_count'")
1147	    if job_count != len(jobs):
1148	        raise _ReconcileInputError(
1149	            f"baseline job_count {job_count} does not match manifest job count {len(jobs)}"
1150	        )
1151	
1152	    results = data["results"]
1153	    if not isinstance(results, list):
1154	        raise _ReconcileInputError("baseline 'results' must be an array")
1155	    if len(results) != job_count:
1156	        raise _ReconcileInputError("baseline 'results' length must equal 'job_count'")
1157	
1158	    seen: set[str] = set()
1159	    actual_succeeded = 0
1160	    for index, entry in enumerate(results):
1161	        where = f"baseline result[{index}]"
1162	        if not isinstance(entry, dict):
1163	            raise _ReconcileInputError(f"{where} must be a JSON object")
1164	        for key in entry:
1165	            if key not in _BASELINE_RESULT_KEYS:
1166	                raise _ReconcileInputError(f"{where} has unknown key {key!r}")
1167	
1168	        if "id" not in entry:
1169	            raise _ReconcileInputError(f"{where} is missing required key 'id'")
1170	        job_id = entry["id"]
1171	        if not isinstance(job_id, str) or not job_id:
1172	            raise _ReconcileInputError(f"{where} 'id' must be a non-empty string")
1173	        if job_id in seen:
1174	            raise _ReconcileInputError(f"duplicate baseline result id {job_id!r}")
1175	        seen.add(job_id)
1176	        if job_id != jobs[index]["id"]:
1177	            raise _ReconcileInputError(
1178	                f"{where} id {job_id!r} does not match manifest id {jobs[index]['id']!r}"
1179	            )
1180	
1181	        if "status" not in entry:
1182	            raise _ReconcileInputError(f"{where} is missing required key 'status'")
1183	        status = entry["status"]
1184	        if status == "succeeded":
1185	            if "output" not in entry:
1186	                raise _ReconcileInputError(f"{where} succeeded result is missing 'output'")
1187	            if "error" in entry:
1188	                raise _ReconcileInputError(f"{where} succeeded result must not contain 'error'")
1189	            _validate_baseline_output(entry["output"], f"{where} output")
1190	            actual_succeeded += 1
1191	        elif status == "failed":
1192	            if "error" not in entry:
1193	                raise _ReconcileInputError(f"{where} failed result is missing 'error'")
1194	            if "output" in entry:
1195	                raise _ReconcileInputError(f"{where} failed result must not contain 'output'")
1196	            _validate_baseline_error(entry["error"], f"{where} error")
1197	        else:
1198	            raise _ReconcileInputError(f"{where} 'status' must be 'succeeded' or 'failed'")

1200	        required_keys = (
1201	            {"id", "status", "output"} if status == "succeeded" else {"id", "status", "error"}
1202	        )
1203	        if set(entry) != required_keys:
1204	            raise _ReconcileInputError(f"{where} has unexpected keys for status {status!r}")
1205	
1206	    if actual_succeeded != succeeded or len(results) - actual_succeeded != failed:
1207	        raise _ReconcileInputError("baseline counters do not match result statuses")

1213	    side: str, arg: str, ctx: _RunContext | None = None

1215	    """Read one reconcile input, returning ``(raw_bytes, base_dir, error_code)``.

1219	    unreadable file or invalid UTF-8, after emitting an ``io_error``.

1249	def _json_equal(expected: object, actual: object) -> bool:
1250	    """Compare parsed JSON ignoring object key order and whitespace.
1251	
1252	    Array order and scalar values (including int-vs-float distinctions and
1253	    numeric precision) are significant.
1254	    """
1255	    if isinstance(expected, dict) and isinstance(actual, dict):
1256	        if set(expected) != set(actual):
1257	            return False
1258	        return all(_json_equal(expected[key], actual[key]) for key in expected)
1259	    if isinstance(expected, list) and isinstance(actual, list):
1260	        return len(expected) == len(actual) and all(
1261	            _json_equal(left, right) for left, right in zip(expected, actual)
1262	        )
1263	    return expected == actual and type(expected) is type(actual)

1535	    if program.num_qubits > MAX_EQUIVALENCE_QUBITS:

1547	def _equivalent(left_arg: str, right_arg: str, ctx: _RunContext | None = None) -> int:
1548	    if left_arg == "-" and right_arg == "-":
1549	        # Standard input cannot serve both sides; do not read it.
1550	        _emit_error(
1551	            "comparison_error",
1552	            "left and right inputs cannot both be read from standard input",
1553	        )
1554	        return 2
1555	
1556	    # Fully validate each side (read, parse, semantics, size) in LEFT, RIGHT
1557	    # order, reporting only the first failure.
1558	    left, error_code = _load_comparison_program("left", left_arg, ctx)
1559	    if left is None:
1560	        return error_code
1561	    right, error_code = _load_comparison_program("right", right_arg, ctx)
1562	    if right is None:
1563	        return error_code
1564	
1565	    if ctx is not None and (guard := _guard_output_conflict(ctx)) is not None:
1566	        return guard
1567	
1568	    left_qubits = left.num_qubits
1569	    right_qubits = right.num_qubits
1570	
1571	    left_clbits, left_measurements = measurement_layout(left)
1572	    right_clbits, right_measurements = measurement_layout(right)
1573	
1574	    if left_qubits != right_qubits:
1575	        result: dict[str, object] = {
1576	            "schema_version": 1,
1577	            "equivalent": False,
1578	            "reason": "qubit_count_mismatch",
1579	            "left_num_qubits": left_qubits,
1580	            "right_num_qubits": right_qubits,
1581	            "distance": None,
1582	            "tolerance": EQUIVALENCE_TOLERANCE,
1583	        }
1584	        return _finish(ctx, result, 0)
1585	
1586	    distance = unitary_distance(unitary_matrix(left), unitary_matrix(right))
1587	
1588	    same_transform = distance <= EQUIVALENCE_TOLERANCE
1589	    same_layout = left_clbits == right_clbits and left_measurements == right_measurements
1590	
1591	    if not same_transform:
1592	        reason = "unitary_distance"
1593	        equivalent = False
1594	    elif not same_layout:
1595	        reason = "measurement_layout_mismatch"
1596	        equivalent = False
1597	    else:
1598	        reason = "equivalent"
1599	        equivalent = True
1600	
1601	    result = {
1602	        "schema_version": 1,
1603	        "equivalent": equivalent,
1604	        "reason": reason,
1605	        "left_num_qubits": left_qubits,
1606	        "right_num_qubits": right_qubits,
1607	        "distance": distance,
1608	        "tolerance": EQUIVALENCE_TOLERANCE,
1609	    }
1610	    return _finish(ctx, result, 0)

1657	def _state_metrics(
1658	    left_arg: str,
1659	    right_arg: str,
1660	    left_noise_arg: str | None,
1661	    right_noise_arg: str | None,
1662	    ctx: _RunContext | None = None,
1663	) -> int:
1664	    # The two sources and the two noise models are four stdin-capable
1665	    # inputs; at most one may be '-'. Detect the conflict without touching
1666	    # standard input.
1667	    stdin_count = sum(
1668	        value == "-"
1669	        for value in (left_arg, left_noise_arg, right_arg, right_noise_arg)
1670	    )
1671	    if stdin_count > 1:
1672	        if left_arg == "-" and right_arg == "-":
1673	            # Keep the historical two-source message byte-for-byte.
1674	            message = "left and right inputs cannot both be read from standard input"
1675	        else:
1676	            message = (
1677	                "at most one of the left source, right source, left noise model and "
1678	                "right noise model can be read from standard input"
1679	            )
1680	        _emit_error("metrics_error", message)
1681	        return 2
1682	
1683	    # Fully validate in left-source, left-model, right-source, right-model
1684	    # order, reporting only the first failure (each tagged with its side).
1685	    left, error_code = _load_program("left", left_arg, ctx)
1686	    if left is None:
1687	        return error_code
1688	    left_model: dict[str, float] | None = None
1689	    if left_noise_arg is not None:
1690	        left_model, error_code = _load_metrics_noise_model("left", left_noise_arg, ctx)
1691	        if left_model is None:
1692	            return error_code
1693	
1694	    right, error_code = _load_program("right", right_arg, ctx)
1695	    if right is None:
1696	        return error_code
1697	    right_model: dict[str, float] | None = None
1698	    if right_noise_arg is not None:
1699	        right_model, error_code = _load_metrics_noise_model("right", right_noise_arg, ctx)
1700	        if right_model is None:
1701	            return error_code
1702	
1703	    if ctx is not None and (guard := _guard_output_conflict(ctx)) is not None:
1704	        return guard
1705	
1706	    # A noisy side evolves a full density matrix (at most MAX_NOISE_QUBITS);
1707	    # a model-less side keeps the 20-qubit state-vector path.
1708	    if left_model is not None and left.num_qubits > MAX_NOISE_QUBITS:
1709	        _emit_error(
1710	            "simulation_error",
1711	            f"noise simulation supports at most {MAX_NOISE_QUBITS} qubits, "
1712	            f"left input has {left.num_qubits}",
1713	            side="left",
1714	        )
1715	        return 3
1716	    if right_model is not None and right.num_qubits > MAX_NOISE_QUBITS:
1717	        _emit_error(
1718	            "simulation_error",
1719	            f"noise simulation supports at most {MAX_NOISE_QUBITS} qubits, "
1720	            f"right input has {right.num_qubits}",
1721	            side="right",
1722	        )
1723	        return 3
1724	
1725	    noisy = left_model is not None or right_model is not None
1726	
1727	    left_state: list[complex] | None = None
1728	    right_state: list[complex] | None = None
1729	    left_rho: list[list[complex]] | None = None
1730	    right_rho: list[list[complex]] | None = None
1731	    if left_model is None:
1732	        left_state = simulate_state_vector(left)
1733	    else:
1734	        left_rho = normalized_density_matrix(evolve_density_matrix(left, left_model))
1735	    if right_model is None:
1736	        right_state = simulate_state_vector(right)
1737	    else:
1738	        right_rho = normalized_density_matrix(evolve_density_matrix(right, right_model))
1739	
1740	    same_qubits = left.num_qubits == right.num_qubits
1741	    reason = "compared" if same_qubits else "qubit_count_mismatch"
1742	
1743	    if not same_qubits:
1744	        fidelity: float | None = None
1745	    elif left_rho is None and right_rho is None:
1746	        fidelity = state_fidelity(left_state, right_state)
1747	    elif left_rho is not None and right_rho is not None:
1748	        fidelity = density_fidelity(left_rho, right_rho)
1749	    elif left_rho is not None:
1750	        fidelity = pure_density_fidelity(right_state, left_rho)
1751	    else:
1752	        fidelity = pure_density_fidelity(left_state, right_rho)
1753	
1754	    left_purity = 1.0 if left_rho is None else density_purity(left_rho)
1755	    right_purity = 1.0 if right_rho is None else density_purity(right_rho)
1756	    left_entropy = (
1757	        single_qubit_entropies(left_state, left.num_qubits)
1758	        if left_rho is None
1759	        else density_single_qubit_entropies(left_rho, left.num_qubits)
1760	    )
1761	    right_entropy = (
1762	        single_qubit_entropies(right_state, right.num_qubits)
1763	        if right_rho is None
1764	        else density_single_qubit_entropies(right_rho, right.num_qubits)
1765	    )
1766	
1767	    if not noisy:
1768	        # No noise model on either side: keep the schema_version 1 payload
1769	        # byte-for-byte identical to the historical command.
1770	        result: dict[str, object] = {
1771	            "schema_version": 1,
1772	            "left_num_qubits": left.num_qubits,
1773	            "right_num_qubits": right.num_qubits,
1774	            "reason": reason,
1775	            "fidelity": fidelity,
1776	            "left_single_qubit_entropy": left_entropy,
1777	            "right_single_qubit_entropy": right_entropy,
1778	        }
1779	    else:
1780	        result = {
1781	            "schema_version": 2,
1782	            "left_num_qubits": left.num_qubits,
1783	            "right_num_qubits": right.num_qubits,
1784	            "reason": reason,
1785	            "left_noise_model": left_model,
1786	            "right_noise_model": right_model,
1787	            "fidelity": fidelity,
1788	            "left_purity": left_purity,
1789	            "right_purity": right_purity,
1790	            "left_single_qubit_entropy": left_entropy,
1791	            "right_single_qubit_entropy": right_entropy,
1792	        }
1793	    return _finish(ctx, result, 0)

"""CLI-independent simulation application core.

Both the command line (``simulate``, ``probabilities`` and
``verify-samples``) and the Python DSL (:class:`~quantum_circuit.circuit.Circuit`)
prepare and validate their own inputs, then delegate here for the actual
work: state evolution, measurement probability aggregation, deterministic
sampling and canonical success-payload assembly.

This module never imports :mod:`quantum_circuit.cli` and performs no file,
standard input, environment or standard stream access. It receives only a
validated :class:`~quantum_circuit.openqasm.Program` together with already
validated sampling parameters and a canonical noise model (as produced by
:func:`quantum_circuit.noise.validate_noise_model` /
:func:`quantum_circuit.noise.parse_noise_model`); failures intrinsic to a
simulation are reported as :class:`SimulationError`.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import math

from .noise import MAX_NOISE_QUBITS, simulate_density_matrix
from .openqasm import Program
from .simulator import (
    measurement_probabilities,
    sample_counts,
    sample_counts_from_probabilities,
    simulate_state_vector,
)

# Probabilities are reported in full; entries this close to 0 are omitted
# and entries this close to 1 are reported as exactly 1. Reported values
# sum to within 1e-12 of 1.
PROBABILITY_ZERO_TOLERANCE = 1e-15
PROBABILITY_ONE_TOLERANCE = 1e-15


class SimulationError(Exception):
    """The prepared circuit cannot be simulated (``simulation_error``).

    The only current case is a noisy circuit beyond the density-matrix
    qubit limit; command-line callers map it to exit code 3.
    """


def noisy_qubit_limit_error(num_qubits: int) -> SimulationError:
    return SimulationError(
        f"noise simulation supports at most {MAX_NOISE_QUBITS} qubits, "
        f"got {num_qubits}"
    )


def snap_probability(value: float) -> float | None:
    """Snap one probability for deterministic output.

    Returns ``None`` when the entry is omitted (magnitude at most
    ``1e-15``), ``1.0`` when it is within ``1e-15`` of 1, and otherwise a
    finite ``float`` clamped to ``(0, 1)`` so simulation round-off can
    never produce an out-of-range value.
    """
    if abs(value) <= PROBABILITY_ZERO_TOLERANCE:
        return None
    if abs(1.0 - value) <= PROBABILITY_ONE_TOLERANCE:
        return 1.0
    return min(1.0, max(0.0, float(value)))


def evolve_basis_probabilities(
    program: Program, noise_model: dict[str, float] | None = None
) -> list[float]:
    """Evolve *program* and return per-basis-state measurement probabilities.

    Without a noise model the final state vector is evolved (the parser
    caps registers at the 20-qubit limit) and amplitudes are squared; with
    one the density matrix is evolved (at most :data:`~quantum_circuit.noise.MAX_NOISE_QUBITS`
    qubits) and its diagonal returned. Raises :class:`SimulationError` when
    a noisy circuit exceeds the density-matrix limit.
    """
    if noise_model is None:
        state = simulate_state_vector(program)
        return [abs(amplitude) ** 2 for amplitude in state]
    if program.num_qubits > MAX_NOISE_QUBITS:
        raise noisy_qubit_limit_error(program.num_qubits)
    return simulate_density_matrix(program, noise_model)


def probability_payload(
    program: Program,
    basis_probabilities: list[float],
    noise_model: dict[str, float] | None = None,
) -> dict[str, object]:
    """Build the deterministic ``probabilities`` success payload.

    The aggregated classical distribution is renormalized by its total
    first, mirroring the normalization the sampling path applies to basis
    probabilities, so simulation round-off (notably density-matrix drift)
    cannot move the reported sum away from 1.
    """
    aggregated = measurement_probabilities(program, basis_probabilities)
    total = math.fsum(aggregated.values())
    probabilities: dict[str, float] = {}
    for key, value in aggregated.items():
        normalized = value / total if total else value
        snapped = snap_probability(normalized)
        if snapped is not None:
            probabilities[key] = snapped

    if noise_model is None:
        return {
            "schema_version": 1,
            "num_qubits": program.num_qubits,
            "num_clbits": program.num_clbits,
            "probabilities": probabilities,
        }
    return {
        "schema_version": 2,
        "num_qubits": program.num_qubits,
        "num_clbits": program.num_clbits,
        "noise_model": noise_model,
        "probabilities": probabilities,
    }


def run_probabilities(
    program: Program, noise_model: dict[str, float] | None = None
) -> dict[str, object]:
    """Evolve *program* and assemble its ``probabilities`` payload."""
    basis_probabilities = evolve_basis_probabilities(program, noise_model)
    return probability_payload(program, basis_probabilities, noise_model)


def run_simulation(
    program: Program,
    shots: int,
    seed: int,
    noise_model: dict[str, float] | None = None,
) -> dict[str, object]:
    """Evolve a prepared circuit and sample it (the ``simulate`` payload).

    Sampling draws from a fresh RNG seeded by *seed*, so equal arguments
    produce equal results and no random state is shared between calls.
    Raises :class:`SimulationError` when a noisy circuit exceeds the
    density-matrix qubit limit.
    """
    if noise_model is None:
        state = simulate_state_vector(program)
        counts = sample_counts(program, state, shots, seed)
        return {
            "schema_version": 1,
            "shots": shots,
            "seed": seed,
            "num_qubits": program.num_qubits,
            "num_clbits": program.num_clbits,
            "counts": counts,
        }
    if program.num_qubits > MAX_NOISE_QUBITS:
        raise noisy_qubit_limit_error(program.num_qubits)
    probabilities = simulate_density_matrix(program, noise_model)
    counts = sample_counts_from_probabilities(program, probabilities, shots, seed)
    return {
        "schema_version": 2,
        "shots": shots,
        "seed": seed,
        "num_qubits": program.num_qubits,
        "num_clbits": program.num_clbits,
        "noise_model": noise_model,
        "counts": counts,
    }

"""The DSL simulation entry points must not depend on the CLI module.

``Circuit.sample`` and ``Circuit.probabilities`` share the CLI-independent
simulation core, so a program that only imports the package must be able
to use them without ``quantum_circuit.cli`` ever being loaded.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import subprocess
import sys


def _run_isolated(source: str) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:
    return subprocess.run(
        [sys.executable, "-c", source],
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        check=False,
    )


def test_sample_and_probabilities_work_without_cli_loaded():
    result = _run_isolated(
        """
import sys

import quantum_circuit
from quantum_circuit import Circuit

assert "quantum_circuit.cli" not in sys.modules

circuit = Circuit(2, 2).h(0).cx(0, 1).measure(0, 0).measure(1, 1)

sample = circuit.sample(shots=200, seed=7)
probabilities = circuit.probabilities()
noisy_sample = circuit.sample(
    shots=128, seed=3, noise_model={"depolarizing": 0.1, "amplitude_damping": 0.05}
)
noisy_probabilities = circuit.probabilities(
    noise_model={"phase_damping": 0.2, "bit_flip": 0.1}
)

# No import of the command line may have happened at any point.
assert "quantum_circuit.cli" not in sys.modules

# Calls are deterministic given the same seed/model.
assert circuit.sample(shots=200, seed=7) == sample
assert circuit.probabilities() == probabilities
assert (
    circuit.sample(
        shots=128,
        seed=3,
        noise_model={"amplitude_damping": 0.05, "depolarizing": 0.1},
    )
    == noisy_sample
)
assert circuit.probabilities({"phase_damping": 0.2, "bit_flip": 0.1}) == noisy_probabilities

# The canonical payload field order matches the documented commands.
assert list(sample) == [
    "schema_version", "shots", "seed", "num_qubits", "num_clbits", "counts",
]
assert list(noisy_sample) == [
    "schema_version", "shots", "seed", "num_qubits", "num_clbits",
    "noise_model", "counts",
]
assert list(noisy_sample["noise_model"]) == ["amplitude_damping", "depolarizing"]

print("ok")
"""
    )
    assert result.returncode == 0, result.stderr
    assert result.stdout.strip() == "ok"


def test_core_module_does_not_import_cli():
    # Importing the shared core never pulls in the command line package.
    result = _run_isolated(
        """
import sys

from quantum_circuit import core

assert "quantum_circuit.cli" not in sys.modules
assert not hasattr(core, "cli")
print("ok")
"""
    )
    assert result.returncode == 0, result.stderr
    assert result.stdout.strip() == "ok"

1	"""Equivalence checking for two noiseless OpenQASM circuits.
2	
3	Two circuits represent the same quantum transformation when their
4	pre-measurement unitaries agree up to a global phase and their measurement
5	layout (classical register width plus qubit-to-clbit mapping) is identical.
6	Register names do not matter.
7	
8	The unitary distance allowing a global phase is
9	
10	    d = min_{|lambda|=1} ||U - lambda V||_F / sqrt(2 * 2**n)
11	      = sqrt(1 - |tr(U^dagger V)| / 2**n)
12	"""
13	
14	from __future__ import annotations
15	
16	import math
17

"""Equivalence checking for two noiseless OpenQASM circuits.

Two circuits represent the same quantum transformation when their
pre-measurement unitaries agree up to a global phase and their measurement
layout (classical register width plus qubit-to-clbit mapping) is identical.
Register names do not matter.

The unitary distance allowing a global phase is

    d = min_{|lambda|=1} ||U - lambda V||_F / sqrt(2 * 2**n)
      = sqrt(1 - |tr(U^dagger V)| / 2**n)
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import math

from .openqasm import Program

# A dense 2**n x 2**n unitary has 4**n entries; 8 qubits is the comparison cap.
MAX_EQUIVALENCE_QUBITS = 8
EQUIVALENCE_TOLERANCE = 1e-10


def measurement_layout(program: Program) -> tuple[int, frozenset[tuple[int, int]]]:
    """Return (classical register width, set of (qubit, clbit) measurements).

    Register names are discarded: only the width and the qubit-to-clbit
    mapping participate in the comparison.
    """
    pairs = frozenset(
        (op.targets[0], op.targets[1])
        for op in program.operations
        if op.kind == "measure"
    )
    return program.num_clbits, pairs


def unitary_distance(u: list[list[complex]], v: list[list[complex]]) -> float:
    """Global-phase-invariant normalized Frobenius distance of two unitaries.

    ``u`` and ``v`` must be square matrices of the same dimension. Returns
    ``min_{|lambda|=1} ||U - lambda V||_F / sqrt(2 * dim)``, a value in
    ``[0, 1]`` that is ``0`` exactly when ``U`` and ``V`` differ only by a
    global phase.

    The minimizer is ``lambda = t / |t|`` with ``t = tr(U^dagger V)``. The
    residual norm is evaluated directly (with compensated summation) rather
    than as ``1 - |t|/dim``: that latter form cancels to a few ulps of
    round-off for nearly identical matrices, which a square root then
    amplifies by orders of magnitude.
    """
    dim = len(u)

    # t = tr(U^dagger V) = sum_{i,j} conj(U[j][i]) * V[j][i], summed with
    # compensated real/imaginary accumulators.
    products = [
        u[j][i].conjugate() * v[j][i]
        for i in range(dim)
        for j in range(dim)
    ]
    trace = complex(math.fsum(z.real for z in products), math.fsum(z.imag for z in products))
    magnitude = math.hypot(trace.real, trace.imag)
    if magnitude == 0.0:
        # No phase aligns anything: U and V are fully orthogonal.
        return 1.0

    # The minimizer of ||U - lambda V|| is lambda = conj(t)/|t|.
    lam = trace.conjugate() / magnitude
    residual_sq = math.fsum(
        abs(u[j][i] - lam * v[j][i]) ** 2
        for i in range(dim)
        for j in range(dim)
    )
    normalized = residual_sq / (2 * dim)
    # Round-off can leave a hair outside [0, 1]; clamp to the valid interval.
    return math.sqrt(min(1.0, max(0.0, normalized)))

"""Static size and feasibility estimation for parsed circuits.

Unlike :mod:`quantum_circuit.simulator`, estimation never evolves the
circuit, samples it, or allocates the exponentially sized state vector,
density matrix or unitary matrix. All figures are derived purely from the
validated :class:`~quantum_circuit.openqasm.Program`.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from .openqasm import Program

# Gates reported in ``gate_counts``, in the fixed output order. The
# schema_version 1 payload (circuits using only the original gate set) keeps
# the historical six-entry mapping byte-identical; as soon as any of the
# controlled gates ``cz``/``crx``/``cry``/``crz`` appears the payload becomes
# schema_version 2 with all ten entries in this fixed order; any of the
# gates ``y``/``z``/``s``/``sdg``/``t``/``tdg``/``swap`` makes it
# schema_version 3 with seventeen entries.
_GATE_ORDER_V1 = ("x", "h", "cx", "rx", "ry", "rz")
_GATE_ORDER_V2 = ("x", "h", "cx", "cz", "rx", "ry", "rz", "crx", "cry", "crz")
_GATE_ORDER_V3 = _GATE_ORDER_V2 + ("y", "z", "s", "sdg", "t", "tdg", "swap")
_V2_GATES = frozenset(_GATE_ORDER_V2) - frozenset(_GATE_ORDER_V1)
_V3_GATES = frozenset(_GATE_ORDER_V3) - frozenset(_GATE_ORDER_V2)

# One complex amplitude/matrix element payload: two doubles (real, imag).
_COMPLEX_BYTES = 16

# mode -> (exponent base of entry_count, qubit limit)
_MODE_TABLE = {
    "state-vector": (2, 20),
    "density-matrix": (4, 10),
    "unitary": (4, 8),
}


def circuit_depth(program: Program) -> int:
    """Compute the circuit depth using an as-soon-as-possible schedule.

    Each gate occupies layer ``1 + max(layer of its qubits)`` and gates are
    processed in source order, so gates on disjoint qubits share a layer.
    Measurements do not contribute to the depth.
    """
    depths = [0] * program.num_qubits
    for op in program.operations:
        if op.kind == "measure":
            continue
        layer = max(depths[qubit] for qubit in op.targets) + 1
        for qubit in op.targets:
            depths[qubit] = layer
    return max(depths, default=0)


def estimate(program: Program, mode: str) -> dict[str, object]:
    """Return the deterministic estimate payload for *program* and *mode*."""
    base, qubit_limit = _MODE_TABLE[mode]

    if any(op.kind in _V3_GATES for op in program.operations):
        schema_version = 3
        gate_order = _GATE_ORDER_V3
    elif any(op.kind in _V2_GATES for op in program.operations):
        schema_version = 2
        gate_order = _GATE_ORDER_V2
    else:
        schema_version = 1
        gate_order = _GATE_ORDER_V1
    gate_counts = {name: 0 for name in gate_order}
    gate_count = 0
    measurement_count = 0
    for op in program.operations:
        if op.kind == "measure":
            measurement_count += 1
        else:
            gate_count += 1
            gate_counts[op.kind] += 1

    entry_count = base**program.num_qubits
    result = {
        "schema_version": schema_version,
        "mode": mode,
        "num_qubits": program.num_qubits,
        "num_clbits": program.num_clbits,
        "gate_count": gate_count,
        "measurement_count": measurement_count,
        "gate_counts": gate_counts,
        "circuit_depth": circuit_depth(program),
        "entry_count": entry_count,
        "complex_payload_bytes": entry_count * _COMPLEX_BYTES,
        "supported": program.num_qubits <= qubit_limit,
        "qubit_limit": qubit_limit,
    }
    return result

1	"""Pauli-product observable expectation values.
2	
3	Used by the ``expectation`` subcommand, which evaluates a list of Pauli
4	products against the final pre-measurement state. Each observable is a
5	tensor product of single-qubit Pauli operators; qubits not listed are
6	acted on by the identity, and an empty operator list is the global
7	identity. Expectations follow ``Tr(rho P)`` (the state-vector path uses
8	``<psi|P|psi>``), so they live in ``[-1, 1]``.
9	
10	The observables document is UTF-8 JSON with the same deterministic,
11	strict structural style as the other JSON inputs: duplicate keys,
12	unknown keys, type substitutions (including booleans posing as
13	integers) and out-of-range counts are all rejected.
14	"""

22	MAX_OBSERVABLES = 100

25	EXPECTATION_TOLERANCE = 1e-15

28	_OBSERVABLE_KEYS = ("id", "operators")

171	        return 0.0

239	    for index, amplitude in enumerate(state):
240	        phase = _pauli_phase(index, parity_bits, y_factor)
241	        value = (state[index ^ flip_bits].conjugate() * phase * amplitude) / (norm * norm)

246	def density_matrix_expectation(
247	    rho: list[list[complex]], operators: list[tuple[int, str]]

250

252	    bit mask of the X/Y sites; *rho* must already be normalized to unit
253	    trace.
254	    """
255	    x_bits, y_bits, z_bits = _phase_bits(operators)
256	    flip_bits = x_bits | y_bits
257	    parity_bits = z_bits | y_bits
258	
259	    if flip_bits == 0:
260	        terms: list[float] = []
261	        for index, row in enumerate(rho):
262	            diagonal = row[index].real
263	            terms.append(
264	                -diagonal if (index & z_bits).bit_count() & 1 else diagonal
265	            )
266	        return math.fsum(terms)
267	
268	    y_factor = _I_POWERS[y_bits.bit_count() & 3]
269	    terms = []
270	    for index, row in enumerate(rho):
271	        phase = _pauli_phase(index, parity_bits, y_factor)
272	        terms.append((row[index ^ flip_bits] * phase).real)
273	    return math.fsum(terms)

"""Deterministic canonical simplification for the OpenQASM 2.0 subset.

The optimizer rewrites the pre-measurement gate sequence into a canonical
form while preserving the circuit's transformation up to a global phase and
keeping the measurement layout (qubit-to-clbit mapping) intact:

* adjacent ``x``/``x``, ``h``/``h``, ``y``/``y``, ``z``/``z`` and
  ``swap``/``swap`` pairs, ``cx``/``cz`` pairs with identical control and
  target, and inverse pairs ``s``/``sdg`` and ``t``/``tdg`` on the same
  qubit cancel ("adjacent" allows intervening gates on disjoint qubits);
* consecutive same-axis ``rx``/``ry``/``rz`` rotations on one qubit merge
  into a single rotation, as do consecutive same-axis ``crx``/``cry``/``crz``
  rotations with identical control and target;
* rotations whose normalized angle has magnitude at most ``1e-12`` are
  deleted;
* gates acting on disjoint qubits are moved past each other until the
  sequence is sorted by a stable key (minimum qubit, maximum qubit, gate
  name and parameter text).

Simplification passes repeat until the sequence reaches a fixed point, so
inputs that differ only in the ordering of independent gates produce
byte-identical output. Single-qubit rotation angles are normalized to
``(-pi, pi]`` (rendering a value at either boundary as ``pi`` when it is
positive). Controlled rotations are normalized to ``(-2*pi, 2*pi]`` instead:
their angle is only ``4*pi``-periodic (a ``2*pi`` shift is *not* a global
phase of the controlled unitary), so ``2*pi`` is kept rather than deleted.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import heapq
import math
from dataclasses import dataclass

from .openqasm import Operation, Program

# Rotations this small (after normalization to (-pi, pi]) act as the
# identity within floating-point precision and are removed.
_ANGLE_EPSILON = 1e-12

_ROTATIONS = ("rx", "ry", "rz")
_CONTROLLED_ROTATIONS = ("crx", "cry", "crz")


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Gate:
    """A pre-measurement gate with its canonical (normalized) angle."""

    kind: str
    qubits: tuple[int, ...]
    angle: float | None = None

    @property
    def qubit_set(self) -> frozenset[int]:
        return frozenset(self.qubits)


def normalize_angle(angle: float) -> float:
    """Reduce *angle* modulo ``2*pi`` into the interval ``(-pi, pi]``.

    Angles already inside the interval are returned untouched so ordinary
    values (e.g. ``0.7``) are not perturbed by floating-point modulo.
    """
    if -math.pi < angle <= math.pi:
        return angle
    reduced = (angle + math.pi) % (2.0 * math.pi) - math.pi
    if reduced == -math.pi:
        return math.pi
    return reduced


def normalize_controlled_angle(angle: float) -> float:
    """Reduce a controlled-rotation angle modulo ``4*pi`` into ``(-2*pi, 2*pi]``.

    A controlled rotation by ``theta + 2*pi`` differs from one by ``theta``
    by more than a global phase (the unshifted rotation picks up a sign on
    the control-1 block only), so the period is ``4*pi`` and ``2*pi`` itself
    is kept. Angles already inside the interval are returned untouched.
    """
    if -2.0 * math.pi < angle <= 2.0 * math.pi:
        return angle
    reduced = (angle + 2.0 * math.pi) % (4.0 * math.pi) - 2.0 * math.pi
    if reduced == -2.0 * math.pi:
        return 2.0 * math.pi
    return reduced


def _format_angle(angle: float) -> str:
    """Render a normalized angle deterministically.

    Uses the shortest decimal representation that round-trips to the same
    float (at most 17 significant digits), which Python writes as plain
    decimal or lowercase scientific notation. Negative zero is written as
    ``0``.
    """
    if angle == 0.0:
        return "0"
    return repr(angle)


def _gate_from_operation(op: Operation) -> Gate:
    if op.kind in ("cx", "cz"):
        return Gate(op.kind, (op.targets[0], op.targets[1]))
    if op.kind == "swap":
        # swap is symmetric in its operands; canonicalize the operand order
        # so swap q[a],q[b] and swap q[b],q[a] share one canonical form.
        return Gate(op.kind, tuple(sorted(op.targets)))
    if op.kind in _ROTATIONS:
        return Gate(op.kind, (op.targets[0],), normalize_angle(op.params[0]))
    if op.kind in _CONTROLLED_ROTATIONS:
        return Gate(
            op.kind,
            (op.targets[0], op.targets[1]),
            normalize_controlled_angle(op.params[0]),
        )
    return Gate(op.kind, (op.targets[0],))


def _sort_key(gate: Gate) -> tuple[int, int, str, str]:
    # Ties (including two commuting gates on the same set, e.g. rz/rx) keep
    # their relative order, which is the dependency order the semantics need.
    parameter = _format_angle(gate.angle) if gate.angle is not None else ""
    return (min(gate.qubits), max(gate.qubits), gate.kind, parameter)


# Inverse pairs that cancel when adjacent on the same qubit.
_INVERSE_PAIRS = (("s", "sdg"), ("sdg", "s"), ("t", "tdg"), ("tdg", "t"))


def _cancels(first: Gate, second: Gate) -> bool:
    """True when *second* immediately follows *first* and both vanish."""
    if first.qubits != second.qubits:
        return False
    if first.kind in ("x", "h", "y", "z", "swap"):
        return first.kind == second.kind
    if first.kind in ("cx", "cz"):
        return second.kind == first.kind
    return (first.kind, second.kind) in _INVERSE_PAIRS


def _merge(first: Gate, second: Gate) -> Gate | None:
    """Merge two same-axis rotations on the same qubits, if applicable.

    Returns the merged :class:`Gate`, or ``None`` when the gates cannot be
    merged. Controlled rotations additionally require identical control and
    target and are normalized onto their ``4*pi`` period.
    """
    if first.kind != second.kind or first.qubits != second.qubits:
        return None
    if first.kind in _ROTATIONS:
        assert first.angle is not None and second.angle is not None
        return Gate(first.kind, first.qubits, normalize_angle(first.angle + second.angle))
    if first.kind in _CONTROLLED_ROTATIONS:
        assert first.angle is not None and second.angle is not None
        return Gate(
            first.kind,
            first.qubits,
            normalize_controlled_angle(first.angle + second.angle),
        )
    return None


def _is_identity_rotation(gate: Gate) -> bool:
    return (
        gate.kind in _ROTATIONS + _CONTROLLED_ROTATIONS
        and gate.angle is not None
        and abs(gate.angle) <= _ANGLE_EPSILON
    )


def _simplify_once(gates: list[Gate]) -> list[Gate] | None:
    """Run one simplification sweep.

    Scans left to right; whenever a gate can cancel or merge with the
    nearest preceding gate that shares a qubit (gates between them acting on
    disjoint qubits are ignored), the rewrite is performed and the scan
    restarts so the newly adjacent gates become visible. Identity rotations
    are dropped on sight. Returns the rewritten list, or ``None`` when no
    rewrite was possible.
    """
    for index in range(len(gates)):
        gate = gates[index]
        if _is_identity_rotation(gate):
            return gates[:index] + gates[index + 1 :]

        for earlier in range(index - 1, -1, -1):
            previous = gates[earlier]
            if previous.qubit_set & gate.qubit_set:
                if _cancels(previous, gate):
                    return gates[:earlier] + gates[earlier + 1 : index] + gates[index + 1 :]
                merged = _merge(previous, gate)
                if merged is not None:
                    return gates[:earlier] + [merged] + gates[earlier + 1 : index] + gates[index + 1 :]
                break
    return None


def _canonical_order(gates: list[Gate]) -> list[Gate]:
    """Return *gates* in canonical order.

    Builds the dependency DAG in which each gate depends on the latest
    preceding gate touching any of the same qubits (so gates on disjoint
    qubits are mutually independent), then takes the unique linear
    extension that minimizes :func:`_sort_key` among all available gates at
    each step. That extension is independent of how independent gates were
    written, which is what makes reordering canonical.
    """
    count = len(gates)
    # predecessors[i]: gates that must precede gate i (share a qubit and come
    # earlier in the source). Only the latest such gate per qubit is needed:
    # transitively it already requires everything before it.
    predecessors: list[set[int]] = [set() for _ in range(count)]
    last_on_qubit: dict[int, int] = {}
    for index, gate in enumerate(gates):
        for qubit in gate.qubits:
            if qubit in last_on_qubit:
                predecessors[index].add(last_on_qubit[qubit])
            last_on_qubit[qubit] = index

    remaining = [len(preds) for preds in predecessors]
    dependents: list[list[int]] = [[] for _ in range(count)]
    for index, preds in enumerate(predecessors):
        for pred in preds:
            dependents[pred].append(index)

    # Heap entries break key ties by original position, preserving the
    # relative (dependency) order of gates that the sort key cannot separate.
    ready: list[tuple[tuple, int]] = [
        (_sort_key(gates[index]), index) for index in range(count) if remaining[index] == 0
    ]
    heapq.heapify(ready)

    ordered: list[Gate] = []
    while ready:
        _, index = heapq.heappop(ready)
        ordered.append(gates[index])
        for dependent in dependents[index]:
            remaining[dependent] -= 1
            if remaining[dependent] == 0:
                heapq.heappush(ready, (_sort_key(gates[dependent]), dependent))
    return ordered


def canonical_gates(operations: tuple[Operation, ...]) -> tuple[tuple[Gate, ...], bool]:
    """Return ``(gates, changed)``: the canonical gate sequence and whether
    any cancellation, merge, deletion or reordering was applied to the
    extracted gates.

    Angle normalization alone (the same gates in the same order) does not
    count as a change.
    """
    gates = [_gate_from_operation(op) for op in operations if op.kind != "measure"]
    changed = False
    while True:
        simplified = _simplify_once(gates)
        if simplified is not None:
            gates = simplified
            changed = True
            continue
        ordered = _canonical_order(gates)
        if ordered != gates:
            gates = ordered
            changed = True
            continue
        return tuple(gates), changed


def _gate_line(gate: Gate) -> str:
    if gate.kind in ("cx", "cz", "swap"):
        return f"{gate.kind} q[{gate.qubits[0]}],q[{gate.qubits[1]}];"
    if gate.kind in _ROTATIONS:
        assert gate.angle is not None
        return f"{gate.kind}({_format_angle(gate.angle)}) q[{gate.qubits[0]}];"
    if gate.kind in _CONTROLLED_ROTATIONS:
        assert gate.angle is not None
        return (
            f"{gate.kind}({_format_angle(gate.angle)}) "
            f"q[{gate.qubits[0]}],q[{gate.qubits[1]}];"
        )
    return f"{gate.kind} q[{gate.qubits[0]}];"


def render(program: Program, gates: tuple[Gate, ...]) -> str:
    """Render the canonical circuit as complete, re-parseable OpenQASM."""
    lines = [
        "OPENQASM 2.0;",
        'include "qelib1.inc";',
        f"qreg q[{program.num_qubits}];",
        f"creg c[{program.num_clbits}];",
    ]
    lines.extend(_gate_line(gate) for gate in gates)
    # Measurements sorted by (clbit, qubit), preserving the qubit-to-clbit
    # mapping from the source program.
    measurements = sorted(
        (op.targets[1], op.targets[0])
        for op in program.operations
        if op.kind == "measure"
    )
    lines.extend(f"measure q[{qubit}] -> c[{clbit}];" for clbit, qubit in measurements)
    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"


def optimize(program: Program) -> tuple[tuple[Gate, ...], bool, str]:
    """Return ``(canonical_gates, changed, canonical_qasm)`` for *program*.

    *changed* is true only when the pre-measurement gate sequence changed
    (cancellation, merge, deletion or reordering); re-rendering the same
    gates with normalized angles does not set it.
    """
    gates, changed = canonical_gates(program.operations)
    return gates, changed, render(program, gates)

2	
3	Enabled via ``simulate --noise-model PATH``. The model is a JSON object with
4	up to four channel keys (probabilities in ``[0, 1]``):
5	
6	- ``amplitude_damping``: |1> decays to |0> with probability gamma.
7	- ``phase_damping``: populations unchanged, off-diagonal entries scaled by
8	  ``1 - gamma``.
9	- ``bit_flip``: ``rho -> (1 - p) rho + p X rho X``.
10	- ``depolarizing``: ``rho -> (1 - p) rho + p I/2`` (the qubit is replaced by
11	  the maximally mixed state with probability ``p``).
12	
13	After every quantum gate, each configured channel is applied to every qubit
14	the gate touched. Qubits of a two-qubit gate (``cx``, ``cz``, ``crx``,
15	``cry``, ``crz``, ``swap``) are processed in ascending index order; channels
16	on one qubit are applied in :data:`CHANNEL_ORDER` order.

32	# below the state-vector register limit.

47	def _object_pairs(pairs: list[tuple[str, object]]) -> dict[str, object]:
48	    result: dict[str, object] = {}
49	    for key, value in pairs:
50	        if key in result:
51	            raise NoiseModelError(f"duplicate key {key!r} in noise model")
52	        result[key] = value

56	def parse_noise_model(text: str) -> dict[str, float]:
57	    """Parse and validate noise-model JSON text.
58	
59	    Returns the configured channels as a mapping in :data:`CHANNEL_ORDER`
60	    order with float probabilities, so models differing only in whitespace
61	    or key order produce identical output. Raises :class:`NoiseModelError`
62	    on any invalid content.
63	    """
64	    try:
65	        data = json.loads(text, object_pairs_hook=_object_pairs, parse_constant=_reject_constant)
66	    except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:
67	        raise NoiseModelError(f"noise model is not valid JSON: {exc}") from None
68	    if not isinstance(data, dict):
69	        raise NoiseModelError("noise model must be a JSON object")
70	    if not data:
71	        raise NoiseModelError("noise model must configure at least one channel")
72	    for key, value in data.items():
73	        if key not in CHANNEL_ORDER:
74	            raise NoiseModelError(f"unknown noise channel {key!r}")
75	        if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, (int, float)):
76	            raise NoiseModelError(f"noise channel {key!r} probability must be a JSON number")
77	        probability = float(value)
78	        if not math.isfinite(probability):
79	            raise NoiseModelError(f"noise channel {key!r} probability must be finite")
80	        if not 0.0 <= probability <= 1.0:
81	            raise NoiseModelError(f"noise channel {key!r} probability must be between 0 and 1")

"""End-to-end tests for the command line interface."""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

from quantum_circuit import __version__, cli

HEADER = 'OPENQASM 2.0;\ninclude "qelib1.inc";\n'
REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent


@pytest.fixture
def write_qasm(tmp_path):
    def _write(body: str, name: str = "circuit.qasm"):
        path = tmp_path / name
        path.write_text(HEADER + body, encoding="utf-8")
        return str(path)

    return _write


@pytest.fixture
def write_bytes(tmp_path):
    def _write(data: bytes, name: str = "circuit.qasm"):
        path = tmp_path / name
        path.write_bytes(data)
        return str(path)

    return _write


# ------------------------------------------------------------- legacy behavior


def test_version_subcommand_prints_version(capsys):
    assert cli.main(["version"]) == 0
    assert capsys.readouterr().out.strip() == __version__


def test_no_subcommand_prints_help(capsys):
    assert cli.main([]) == 0
    out = capsys.readouterr().out
    assert "usage:" in out
    assert "simulate" in out


def test_help_flag_exits_zero(capsys):
    with pytest.raises(SystemExit) as info:
        cli.main(["--help"])
    assert info.value.code == 0
    assert "usage:" in capsys.readouterr().out


def test_simulate_help_flag(capsys):
    with pytest.raises(SystemExit) as info:
        cli.main(["simulate", "--help"])
    assert info.value.code == 0
    out = capsys.readouterr().out
    assert "--shots" in out and "--seed" in out


# --------------------------------------------------------------- success output


def test_success_json_shape_and_field_order(write_qasm):
    path = write_qasm(
        "qreg q[2];\ncreg c[2];\nh q[0];\ncx q[0],q[1];\n"
        "measure q[0] -> c[0];\nmeasure q[1] -> c[1];\n"
    )
    assert cli.main(["simulate", path, "--shots", "50", "--seed", "7"]) == 0


def test_success_payload(write_qasm, capsys):
    path = write_qasm(
        "qreg q[2];\ncreg c[2];\nh q[0];\ncx q[0],q[1];\n"
        "measure q[0] -> c[0];\nmeasure q[1] -> c[1];\n"
    )
    rc = cli.main(["simulate", path, "--shots", "50", "--seed", "7"])
    captured = capsys.readouterr()
    assert rc == 0
    raw = captured.out
    assert raw.endswith("\n")
    assert raw.count("\n") == 1

    data = json.loads(raw)
    assert data["schema_version"] == 1
    assert (data["shots"], data["seed"]) == (50, 7)
    assert (data["num_qubits"], data["num_clbits"]) == (2, 2)
    assert sum(data["counts"].values()) == 50

    # Field order is part of the contract.
    assert list(data) == ["schema_version", "shots", "seed", "num_qubits", "num_clbits", "counts"]
    counts = data["counts"]
    assert list(counts) == sorted(counts)


def test_defaults_are_1024_shots_and_seed_zero(write_qasm, capsys):
    path = write_qasm("qreg q[1];\ncreg c[1];\nmeasure q[0] -> c[0];\n")
    assert cli.main(["simulate", path]) == 0
    data = json.loads(capsys.readouterr().out)
    assert data["shots"] == 1024 and data["seed"] == 0
    assert data["counts"] == {"0": 1024}


def test_repeated_runs_are_byte_identical(write_qasm, capsys):
    path = write_qasm(
        "qreg q[3];\ncreg c[3];\nh q[0];\nh q[1];\ncx q[1],q[2];\n"
        "measure q[0] -> c[0];\nmeasure q[1] -> c[1];\nmeasure q[2] -> c[2];\n"
    )
    outputs = set()
    for _ in range(3):
        assert cli.main(["simulate", path, "--shots", "128", "--seed", "123"]) == 0
        outputs.add(capsys.readouterr().out)

"""Final-state comparison metrics for two circuits.

Both circuits evolve from the all-zero initial state (terminal measurements
are ignored, matching :func:`simulate_state_vector` and the density-matrix
path). When neither side carries a noise model both final states are pure
state vectors and the metrics are the squared overlap
``|<left|right>|^2`` plus, for each side, the per-qubit von Neumann entropy
of the reduced density matrix.

With a noise model on either side, that side evolves as a full density
matrix. The comparison metrics then generalize to:

- the squared Uhlmann fidelity ``(Tr sqrt(sqrt(rho) sigma sqrt(rho)))**2``,
  which equals ``|<psi|phi>|^2`` when both states are pure and
  ``<psi|rho|psi>`` when exactly one is mixed;
- the purity ``Tr(rho**2)`` of each density matrix (1 for a pure state);
- the same per-qubit binary von Neumann entropy, computed from each side's
  (possibly mixed) reduced density matrix.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import math

# Values within this distance of 0 or 1 are reported as exactly 0 or 1.
SNAP_TOLERANCE = 1e-15

# Eigenvalues of the numerically rebuilt product ``sqrt(rho) sigma
# sqrt(rho)`` below this absolute floor are treated as exact zeros. Round-off
# leaves phantom eigenvalues of order 1e-17 (NumPy) to 1e-16 (the pure-Python
# Jacobi path) in null subspaces; kept as-is their square roots would inject
# amplified noise into the fidelity root sum.
_EIGENVALUE_NOISE_FLOOR = 1e-13


def _snap01(value: float) -> float:
    """Clamp *value* to [0, 1] and snap to the endpoints within tolerance.

    Guarantees a finite, non-negative-zero result: values no larger than
    ``SNAP_TOLERANCE`` in magnitude become ``0.0`` and values within
    ``SNAP_TOLERANCE`` of 1 become ``1.0``.
    """
    value = min(1.0, max(0.0, value))
    if abs(value) <= SNAP_TOLERANCE:
        return 0.0
    if abs(1.0 - value) <= SNAP_TOLERANCE:
        return 1.0
    return value


def state_fidelity(left: list[complex], right: list[complex]) -> float:
    """Return ``|<left|right>|^2`` of the two normalized state vectors.

    Both states must have the same dimension. The states are renormalized
    explicitly so round-off in the simulation cannot push the result out
    of [0, 1].
    """
    norm_left = math.fsum(abs(amplitude) ** 2 for amplitude in left)
    norm_right = math.fsum(abs(amplitude) ** 2 for amplitude in right)
    products = [a.conjugate() * b for a, b in zip(left, right)]
    inner = complex(
        math.fsum(z.real for z in products),
        math.fsum(z.imag for z in products),
    )
    fidelity = (inner.real**2 + inner.imag**2) / (norm_left * norm_right)
    return _snap01(fidelity)


def normalized_density_matrix(rho: list[list[complex]]) -> list[list[complex]]:
    """Return *rho* divided by its trace (a fresh, exactly unit-trace copy).

    Every configured noise channel is trace preserving in exact arithmetic,

    ulps, just as state-vector evolution drifts the norm. All density-matrix
    metrics assume a normalized state, so callers normalize once, mirroring
    the explicit renormalization :func:`state_fidelity` applies to vectors.
    """

Usage: python3 /tmp/qcs_golden.py <label>
Writes /tmp/qcs-golden/snapshot-<label>.json. Workspace files live at a
fixed path so absolute paths embedded in error messages stay comparable.

import os
import subprocess
import sys

HEADER = 'OPENQASM 2.0;\ninclude "qelib1.inc";\n'


def w(name: str, content: str | bytes) -> str:
    path = os.path.join(WORK, name)
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(path), exist_ok=True)
    if isinstance(content, bytes):
        with open(path, "wb") as handle:
            handle.write(content)

    label = sys.argv[1]
    setup()
    repo_root = "/mnt/c/dbsvace/vo5/B/task020"
    scenarios = build_scenarios()

    # Generate baselines from actual command output.
    def run_batch(manifest_name):
        proc = subprocess.run(
            [sys.executable, "-m", "quantum_circuit.cli", "batch-simulate", os.path.join(WORK, manifest_name)],
            capture_output=True, text=True, cwd=repo_root,
        )
        return proc.stdout

    w("baseline_ok.json", run_batch("batch_ok.json"))
    # Baseline for batch_fail: take actual output but flip the first task to
    # force a mismatch; instead just snapshot the actual fail output and use
    # it as an identical baseline (recon_fail needs a mismatch -> tweak one id status).
    fail_out = run_batch("batch_fail.json")
    fail_data = json.loads(fail_out)
    # Corrupt baseline: change the message of one failed task -> error_mismatch.
    for entry in fail_data["results"]:
        if entry["status"] == "failed":
            entry["error"] = dict(entry["error"])
            entry["error"]["message"] = entry["error"]["message"] + " (baseline)"
            break
    w("baseline_fail.json", json.dumps(fail_data))

    snapshot = {}
    for scenario in scenarios:
        proc = subprocess.run(
            [sys.executable, "-m", "quantum_circuit.cli", *scenario["argv"]],
            input=scenario["stdin"],
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
            cwd=repo_root,
        )
        snapshot[scenario["name"]] = {
            "argv": scenario["argv"],
            "rc": proc.returncode,
            "stdout": proc.stdout,
            "stderr": proc.stderr,
        }
    os.makedirs("/tmp/qcs-golden", exist_ok=True)
    with open(f"/tmp/qcs-golden/snapshot-{label}.json", "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        json.dump(snapshot, handle, indent=2, sort_keys=True)
    print(f"recorded {len(snapshot)} scenarios -> /tmp/qcs-golden/snapshot-{label}.json")

"""Structured command failures shared by input preparation and pure logic.

The command layer speaks about failures as data rather than exceptions:
:class:`CommandFailure` carries exactly the fields that become the
single-line stderr JSON document (``error``/``message`` and, for a few
inputs, ``input``/``line``/``column``) together with the process exit code.

This module performs no file system, standard input or standard stream
access, so preparation and pure computation can build failures without
depending on the terminal.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class CommandFailure(Exception):
    """A failed command step as a serializable payload plus exit code.

    Subclassing :class:`Exception` lets pure helpers raise it through
    call stacks while preparation code normally constructs and returns it.
    """

    error: str
    message: str
    exit_code: int
    side: str | None = None
    line: int | None = None
    column: int | None = None

    def to_payload(self) -> dict[str, object]:
        """Return the canonical stderr JSON object (ordered fields)."""
        payload: dict[str, object] = {"error": self.error}
        if self.side is not None:
            payload["input"] = self.side
        payload["message"] = self.message
        if self.line is not None:
            payload["line"] = self.line
            payload["column"] = self.column
        return payload

85	def _entropy_from_qubit_block(
86	    rho00: float, rho11: float, off_re: float, off_im: float
87	) -> float:
88	    """Binary entropy of the 2x2 Hermitian block ``[[rho00, z], [z*, rho11]]``.
89	
90	    ``z`` is supplied as real/imaginary parts. The two eigenvalues of the
91	    block are computed directly; zero (or slightly negative) eigenvalues do
92	    not contribute.
93	    """
94	    off_magnitude_sq = off_re**2 + off_im**2
95	    half_trace = (rho00 + rho11) / 2
96	    half_diff = (rho00 - rho11) / 2
97	    spread = math.sqrt(half_diff**2 + off_magnitude_sq)
98	
99	    entropy = 0.0
100	    for eigenvalue in (half_trace - spread, half_trace + spread):
101	        # Round-off can leave a hair outside [0, 1]; zero (or slightly
102	        # negative) eigenvalues do not contribute.
103	        if eigenvalue > 0.0:
104	            entropy -= eigenvalue * math.log2(eigenvalue)
105	    return _snap01(entropy)
106	
107	
108	def single_qubit_entropies(state: list[complex], num_qubits: int) -> list[float]:
109	    """Return the per-qubit reduced-state von Neumann entropies (base 2).
110	
111	    Entry ``i`` is ``S(rho_i) = -sum lambda log2(lambda)`` where ``rho_i``
112	    is the reduced density matrix of qubit ``i`` (qubit ``i`` lives in bit
113	    ``i`` of the basis index) and zero eigenvalues do not contribute. A
114	    product state gives all zeros; each qubit of a Bell pair gives 1.
115	    """
116	    entropies: list[float] = []
117	    for qubit in range(num_qubits):
118	        bit = 1 << qubit
119	        diag0_terms: list[float] = []
120	        diag1_terms: list[float] = []
121	        off_re_terms: list[float] = []
122	        off_im_terms: list[float] = []
123	        for index, amplitude in enumerate(state):
124	            if index & bit:
125	                diag1_terms.append(amplitude.real**2 + amplitude.imag**2)
126	            else:
127	                diag0_terms.append(amplitude.real**2 + amplitude.imag**2)
128	                product = amplitude * state[index | bit].conjugate()
129	                off_re_terms.append(product.real)
130	                off_im_terms.append(product.imag)
131	
132	        entropies.append(
133	            _entropy_from_qubit_block(
134	                math.fsum(diag0_terms),
135	                math.fsum(diag1_terms),
136	                math.fsum(off_re_terms),
137	                math.fsum(off_im_terms),
138	            )
139	        )
140	    return entropies
141	
142	
143	def density_purity(rho: list[list[complex]]) -> float:
144	    """Return ``Tr(rho**2)`` of a normalized density matrix.
145	
146	    For a Hermitian matrix this is the squared Frobenius norm
147	    ``sum |rho_ij|**2``; a pure state gives 1 and the maximally mixed state
148	    of ``n`` qubits gives ``2**-n``.
149	    """
150	    total = math.fsum(abs(entry) ** 2 for row in rho for entry in row)
151	    return _snap01(total)
152	
153	
154	def density_single_qubit_entropies(
155	    rho: list[list[complex]], num_qubits: int
156	) -> list[float]:
157	    """Per-qubit reduced-state binary entropies for a (possibly mixed) state.
158	
159	    Same convention as :func:`single_qubit_entropies`, but the reductions
160	    are taken from the full density matrix, so the result also reflects
161	    classical/mixed-state entropy rather than only entanglement.
162	    """
163	    entropies: list[float] = []
164	    size = len(rho)
165	    for qubit in range(num_qubits):
166	        bit = 1 << qubit
167	        diag0_terms: list[float] = []
168	        diag1_terms: list[float] = []
169	        off_re_terms: list[float] = []
170	        off_im_terms: list[float] = []
171	        for index in range(size):
172	            if index & bit:
173	                diag1_terms.append(rho[index][index].real)
174	            else:
175	                diag0_terms.append(rho[index][index].real)
176	                entry = rho[index][index | bit]
177	                off_re_terms.append(entry.real)
178	                off_im_terms.append(entry.imag)
179	
180	        entropies.append(
181	            _entropy_from_qubit_block(
182	                math.fsum(diag0_terms),
183	                math.fsum(diag1_terms),
184	                math.fsum(off_re_terms),
185	                math.fsum(off_im_terms),
186	            )
187	        )
188	    return entropies
189
